With the girls sitting quietly next to their teenage caretaker and thoroughly occupied, Inzili carefully set the plastic case down and opened it to reveal four disposable auto-injectors. Each label was identical and featured a prominent age range, but she had medical training and knew it was only a guideline that was there for the benefit of the untrained masses. First was Akisa who was completely oblivious to what was going on, her arm was confiscated without struggle and the injector was pressed to the tender scales on her arm.

"Here you go," Inzili cooed as she activated the device, "look at me."

Her small patient blinked and looked up at her just as the device stung with metal clatter, the pain took only a second to register and her lower lip started to quiver as the tears came.

"All done! Very good!"

Akisa disagreed, blubbering out gibberish and hiding her face with both hands. She even refused to be coddled, scooting away to the far corner out of reach from the adult that betrayed her to sob quietly alone. Her sister seemed irritated by the noise, showing her teeth and growling a warning to make sure her displeasure was known. With a smooth motion her arm was confiscated and received the same treatment, the loud clatter was followed by a brief moment of silence as she examined the freshly wounded spot. Her mouth opened and she wailed loudly before scurrying away from her mother with a furious glare, but when her display wasn't well-received she screamed in rage and threw a fit far out of arm's reach.

"Nuva, stop this."

Furious and hurt the girl arched her back and screamed loudly at her mother, the dull blue scales on her face had shifted to purplish-red from the fury, she swatted at the open air between them.

"You are not acting like big girl," Inzili chided in her mate's language, "what would your father say?"

"Nabah wah!" the girl responded, pounding her fists on the bed. Then she barked in protest before screaming again.

"I think this means that she's still angry," Jhoka giggled, stealing a glance at the angry runt. "My turn now?"

Grabbing a third injector Inzili nodded and said, "this will hurt far less than it seems, they are not used to pain."

"Soft children," the younger female mumbled with an outstretched arm.

"When you're a mother you raise yours however you wish," she shot back, stamping the injector to the tough scales without mercy.

For a moment it seemed like the needle hadn't gone deep enough, but when Jhoka pulled her arm back it was clear the injection had gone as expected. This would be the first of three she would need, her immune system would be taught in stages for maximum results. She didn't know that though. Rubbing her arm she looked at the tiny hole that pierced through her tough hide, topped with a bead of her own blood, instinct told her to lap at it and she gave in.

"You will feel weak soon, then tired, then feverish. This will pass, and you'll thank me when you're never sick from illnesses that take unprotected children all the time."

Nodding quickly she glanced back at the girls and held out her hand. "They probably won't."

"I can fix this," she sighed, unzipping her jumpsuit and readying a breast.

With a furious huff her daughter scurried close enough to find herself scooped up and held tight, but the unruly child settled almost immediately just as expected. Feeding her daughter brought some relief to the growing soreness and let Inzili release some of the stored tension in her shoulders.

"Does that feel good?"

She nodded as she caressed her daughter's head. "You'll find out someday, but yes it does."

"How?"

"You can't know until you're a mother, like many things it is a small relief that comes from hard work."

"Should I go find Jade for her?"

"No, I have enough for both today."

Jhoka nodded and smiled, the idea of motherhood appealed to her sometimes and seeing the little creature suckling happily made it seem easier than she knew it was. Her kind was destined to be feral little beasts for several moons and she hoped to mate a human to get a relaxed, well-behaved child like Nuva. Though sometimes it seemed so odd that something like her came from him, she was visually similar to her mother in most ways.

"I wonder how long I have until I am ready again, can I raise my own with yours? Would you let me have this honor?"

Waving the question away Inzili sarcastically said, "no, you can only raise your daughters in the corner."

"I am serious."

Smirking at the young female Inzili put a hand on her knee. "Giving my daughters a normal life would be wonderful, they would need a friend. After all, you are big sister to them and it would be good to have your child grow up with them. Just don't rush."

"If it happens I won't complain," Jhoka replied with a shrug, the idea mostly theoretical at that moment.

An acceptable answer for their kind, it was expected for a young female to accept their duty to produce an heir and raise her with or without a father. Though it would be preferable if the father was out of the picture since it seemed like the girl was enthusiastic about finding a human to bed. One human, her human, was more than enough for their tiny vessel in Inzili's opinion, she would probably need to steer the young female toward a more suitable mate and perhaps toward one of their own kind! Regardless of the pick it would take some effort to convince her stubborn human to play nice, Jade would inevitably agree if it meant more domestic aspects to their lives.

"When I became ready I wouldn't leave him alone, I needed him every second until I woke up one morning and felt that my body was different. I knew. Then I hid on the ship and ate, I ate and ate, he even brought home a giant slab of meat."

"Oh that sounds so wonderful."

She grinned and nodded. "It was, I kept myself full for two whole days."

Jhoka swooned and sighed as she thought of having her own doting mate bring her a fresh kill. "A good start for any mother, did you still...?"

"No, nothing like that. I kissed him and was affectionate, but it is a strange time and had no interest. I felt irritated and hostile toward Jade, she kept her distance."

There was probably a biological reason for that sudden shift in demeanor, but it worked itself out in the end. Those were simpler times, if she had known how much trouble she'd be in maybe she would have... No, she would have made the same choice. Looking down at her sleepy daughter reminded her how precious she was no matter how much of a handful she proved to be, but that was mostly Jade's problem anyway.

"I like watching you with them. You have a strong bond, it means something that is real..." Jhoka trailed off and looked out the window. "Sometimes it seems like our kind mates because we are expected, there is not much love shared."

"You will find this is not unique to us," Inzili laughed, shifting her position as Akisa crawled close. "This is a common thing among many, including the humans."

"I was hoping to escape as many of our ways as I can," she mumbled, thinking of the complex and unspoken rules of her village.

Tucking Nuva into a roll of covers took priority for a moment, but afterward she pulled her other daughter up and got her settled. "Jhoka, you will learn to miss your home very soon. What I came from was awful, you know what I am, but you still have love here. There are times when even I miss my little hole under a tree that I made for myself, living on the outskirts of my people, hiding from the hunters who would take my scales for sport."

"That sounds..."

"Like I am crazy? I know. So what would that make you if you never wanted to see your father again? Khojaewa?"

"Would it be so strange if I didn't want to see her again?"

"Why?"

Jhoka scowled and shook her head. "Out of everyone in the village I had hope she would have been kinder to me. Her youngest, Yusha..." she first trailed off before looking at the other woman, "do you remember her?"

"Yes."

"At the festival for the Goddess, I expected to have a silver ring on my tail the same year Yusha got her own in front of everyone. I saw their looks, they glanced at me and I smiled as brightly as I could to hide the shame. I said nice things, I did all the right things, but it was obvious that my closest friend's ambition was too much to look past to see me."

"Maybe she..." the older female stopped herself, knowing the words ahead were untrue. No, what had happened was Khojaewa's rising star couldn't afford to carry the local idiot if it hoped to continue. With that her opinion of the mighty alpha that took them into her home had diminished, the mystery of the lost love was quite different than what she had imagined. Such a public humiliation was either a gross miscalculation or a deliberate snub, either way it was an unacceptable blow to Jhoka's already fragile standing among the village.

After a long silence Jhoka turned and looked square at Inzili again. "At least I'm not barren. Maybe I should laugh at Khojaewa's poor choice?"

"That's unkind of you."
